title: About the Legonizer
intro: The Legonizer is a research tool from the VCity team of the LIRIS lab. It turns 3D city models into brick models for augmented physical models: a table, white bricks, a projector and a screen.

privacy.title: Your data stays with you
privacy.body: Everything runs in your browser. Your 3D files are never uploaded. Plate links and QR codes carry the plate inside the link itself.

method.title: How it works
method.heights: For every stud, the Legonizer measures the height of the city below it by casting a ray from above, then turns that height into a number of bricks.
method.legacy: The Legacy preset reproduces the UD-Viz 4.6.1 widget exactly, including its known limits, so researchers can compare results. Other options are improvements you choose.
method.bricks: The bricks are chosen layer by layer for each plate: as few bricks as possible, never crossing a plate edge, and overlapping the seams below so the model holds together.

paper.title: The research
paper.citation: C. Le Bihan Gautier, J. Delanoy, G. Gesquière. Représentation de l'évolution urbaine à travers une maquette tangible de territoires. Journées Françaises de l'Informatique Graphique (JFIG), Strasbourg, October 2024. hal-04924304. Licence CC0 1.0.

licences.title: Licences and credits
licences.data: Demo data: an invented sample district generated by the Legonizer, same licence as this site.

files.title: About the files
files.csv: Height matrix (CSV): one line per row of studs, from north to south; one value per stud, from west to east, separated by semicolons; each value is a number of bricks.
files.ldraw: LDraw model: 1 stud = 20 LDraw units, a brick is 24 units high, colour 15 (white).
files.project: Project file: input file names and fingerprints, area, settings, app version and heights. Opening it gives identical files.
